blocks.x: If you were tasked with finding the best pizza in the world, educated guessing would certainly land you a couple of spots on the Family Feud board. There's of course the very birthplace of pizza, Italy, where some of the best pizzaiolos in the world still live and train in hubs ranging from Rome to Caserta. Naturally, your mind might wander to New York City, the city that put the culinary export on the map, thanks to the waves of Italian immigrant communities who arrived in the early 20th century. Today, you can hardly throw a stone in New York without hitting one of the over 2,000 spots slinging slices and serving pies across all five of its boroughs. But who among us would've offered São Paulo, or Tokyo, even, as the amazing pizza cities they are?

Setting out to find the cream of the crop when it comes to the very best pizza in the world is the tall task that the international guide 50 Top Pizza sets out to tackle each year. Leaving no pizza stone unturned, the results usually shake out as a healthy mix of the usual suspects and the odd dark horse, with the number one spot on the 2026 list snatched by a first-time world champion in West London. For these celebrated and the sleeper hits, both nonna-approved authenticity and boundary-pushing experimentation, below is the 2026 list of the best pizza in the entire world, according to the pros at 50 Top Pizza.

blocks.x: London's Napoli on the Road was named the best pizza in the world, according to the team at 50 Top Pizza.

The golden standard for what pizza should be is generally set at the classic Neapolitan style—a puffy, leopard-spotted crust filled with pockets of warm air and topped with simple ingredients that sing with freshness. At this London pizzeria, that platonic ideal gets a remix for the better, and according to the panel at 50 Top Pizza, Napoli on the Road serves as a “reference point for those looking for a modern interpretation of Neapolitan tradition, built with talent, ambition, and vision.” There are now three locations—in Chiswick, Richmond, and Soho—throughout the city, and all offer the same dynamic approach to pizza-making that chef Michele Pascarella sought to craft. For a taste of their best riffing, try the Wild Marinara that pairs semi-dry cherry tomatoes with taggiasche olives, Cetara anchovy filets, and wild garlic pesto. Bring your vegan friends too, as this shop offers four plant-based pies, including a version of the zucchini pizza with vegan stracciatella and fried mint.

blocks.x: New York City's Una Pizza Napoletana is the result of chef Anthony Mangieri’s "decades-long pursuit of pizza.”

Learning the lore behind this Lower East Side pizza spot will only deepen your appreciation for their meticulously crafted pies. The saga begins 30 years ago in Point Pleasant Beach, New Jersey, and ventures over the years to the East Village and San Francisco before finally landing at the restaurant's current home in the LES, the one and only “expression of Anthony Mangieri’s decades-long pursuit of pizza.” The payoff of those 30 years spent experimenting, playing with ingredient permutations, and cultivating an international following is the dedicated pizzaiolo's delightfully airy where the devil is in the dough. Should you land one of their coveted reservations, make sure to choose wisely and savor well—the restaurant reserves exactly one pie for each guest present at the reservation. The menu is minimal, with just six pizzas to choose from: the Marinara, the Margherita, the Bianca, the Filetti, the Cosacca, and a rotating special. Having taken home the top spot on the 50 Top Pizza list three years in a row and coming in a respectable second place in this edition, Una Pizza Napoletana defends its aptonym well.

blocks.x: In Milan, the pizza menu comes with cocktail and wine pairings.

It’s not often that you come across a pizza restaurant that offers tasting menus with wine and cocktail pairings, yet Confine promises just that (along with à la carte options for those feeling a little less peckish). The wine list is 500-bottles strong, focusing on whites from Campania, and there are some great alcohol-free options, too, including cider and kombucha. A glass-fronted open-plan kitchen allows diners to watch the pizzaiolo hard at work, expertly twirling and topping pizzas such as Popeye, a favorite made with spinach sautéed in Normandy butter, Parmesan, marinated egg yolk, steak tartare, and black truffle. The restaurant is housed in a former ironmongery
